purpose: Whether a signing request whose result is uncertain may be recovered, and only with the identical digest. Recovery never creates a second signature over different bytes and never implies chain confirmation.
authority: secure-sign-service-rs (gateway-signer-custody-backend) owns the wire shape; neo-os-services/workers/neo-signer is its only platform consumer

operationId.description: platform operation the signing request belongs to

requestDigest.description: SHA-256 of the exact bytes presented for signing

method.description: signing method requested (for example sign_n3_tx, sign_evm_tx)

network.description: NetworkIdentity name the request is bound to

identity.description: custody key identity or caller identity the request was issued under

issuedAt.description: unix milliseconds the original request was accepted

state.description: recovery classification of the original request

evidence.description: reference to the signing audit record that supports the classification

states.recoverable: the same operationId, method, network, identity and requestDigest were recorded; the original signature may be returned again
states.conflicting: a request with the same operationId but a different digest, method, network or identity exists; operator review is required before any signature is released
states.expired: the original request is past its validity and no signature may be recovered
states.unknown: no durable record of the request exists; the caller must treat the signing attempt as never made

invariants: recovery returns only the signature over the original requestDigest; a different digest is a new request under a new operationId
conflicting claims are never resolved automatically
a recovered signature is signing evidence only and never implies submission or chain confirmation (neoos.transaction-outcome owns that)
adoption: vocabulary published 2026-09-21 from the target architecture's SigningRecovery domain; the custody gateway's recovery protocol rework in progress binds to these states and fields (finding A-20)
